author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
The US has conducted a non-nuclear underground experiment to enhance its ability to detect low-yield nuclear explosions that it explicitly linked with a test that Washington suspects China carried out in 2020 – an accusation Beijing denies.
The US Department of Energy announced on Wednesday that the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) conducted a “subsurface, non-nuclear chemical high-explosive” experiment at the Nevada National Security Site, which it said aimed to “increase the...
title: US blast simulation targets China’s alleged secret nuclear testing

author: Nayan Seth
description:
US Republican Senator Steve Daines, a close aide to President Donald Trump and a key interlocutor between Washington and Beijing, has called on the two capitals to stay engaged and “not retreat” over differences on issues including rare earth supply chains.
Daines told the South China Morning Post that both sides still had issues that predated Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington last week and that they would continue working on them after the summit.
“So that’s again why...
title: ‘No retreat’: Key Trump ally urges continued US-China engagement on rare earths

author: Han Li
description:
Amid intensifying competition in the AI technology race, US authorities have arrested a California technology company owner accused of using Malaysia and Singapore as transit points to circumvent US export controls and send more than US$300 million worth of restricted computer servers to China.
Greg Lui, 38, also known as Yiu Kong Lui, of San Gabriel, was arrested on Thursday and charged with conspiracy to violate US export controls, outbound smuggling and conspiracy to commit money laundering,...
title: US man arrested over alleged $300 million scheme to smuggle Nvidia AI servers to China

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva named China as a possible partner in his critical minerals plans, three days before Sunday’s closely fought election.
Lula told Flow, one of the country’s most-watched podcasts, on Thursday evening that Brazil should stop shipping out raw ore. “We want to transform them here in Brazil,” he said of the minerals.
Asked whether China fit into his plans, Lula said it could be a partner “bringing technology to us”, as could the United States. “[Donald]...
title: Brazil’s Lula hails ‘bold’ Chinese investors as rival pitches rare earths to Trump

author: Teresa Elena Frontado,Igor Patrick
description:
Panama’s comptroller general said on Friday that his office would send prosecutors more audit material on former executives of CK Hutchison’s local subsidiary next week, as part of a criminal investigation into the Hong Kong conglomerate’s annulled Panama Canal ports concession.
Speaking at the Atlantic Council in Washington, Anel Flores said prosecutors had requested documents concerning Panama Ports Company (PPC), the operator of the Balboa and Cristobal terminals at either end of the canal...
title: Panama auditor targets ex-port regulators and CK Hutchison’s executives in canal probe

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Taiwan’s Coast Guard Administration (CGA) used water cannons to expel a mainland Chinese fishing vessel near Dongsha Island, authorities said on Friday.
The incident occurred on October 1, 27 nautical miles east of the Taiwanese-controlled Dongsha Island, also called Pratas Island, in the South China Sea, the agency revealed.
The CGA’s patrol vessel Yunlin directed its water cannon towards the fishing boat Jin Sha’s wheelhouse for about 90 seconds after initially spraying water into the air for...
title: Taiwan coastguard uses water cannons to warn off mainland Chinese fishing vessel

author: Dewey Sim,Khushboo Razdan
description:
US President Donald Trump is planning to attend the Asean summit next month, the South China Morning Post understands, as Washington vies with Beijing for influence in the region.
If the trip happens, Trump’s appearance at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations meeting, expected to run from November 16-18 in Manila, will be his second consecutive appearance at the gathering during this term.
Trump was in Kuala Lumpur for Asean last year and in Manila for the meeting in 2017.
Sources told the...
title: Donald Trump is planning trip to the Philippines for Asean summit

author: Eve Qiao
description:
China is ramping up its efforts to bring young Americans to China, and ready to be seen as a country concerned with environmental protection, lifting people out of poverty, protecting minority cultures and building the technology of the future.
During his trip to the United States last week, Chinese President Xi Jinping said his country aimed to welcome 100,000 young Americans on exchange or study trips over the next five years.
That builds on an earlier target announced in 2023 that set the...
title: If young US people accept Xi’s invitation to China, what will Beijing show them?

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven of the most interesting and important news stories covering global relations from the past few weeks. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Trump condemns ‘sick conspiracy’ against AI, says he is only guardrail needed

US President Donald Trump downplayed growing concerns about artificial intelligence, claiming America already has guardrails to regulate the industry and warning that casting doubt on development only benefits...
title: ‘America is back’, AI ‘conspiracy’, China’s Laos deal: 7 global relations reads

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China has set up several new institutions at military academies to train specialists in hi-tech and discipline inspection as the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) works towards its centennial modernisation goals.
The College of Unmanned and Intelligent Engineering, the College of Combat Support NCOs (Non-Commissioned Officers) and the College of Equipment Support NCOs were established within the PLA Army Engineering University on Wednesday.
On the same day, the National Defence University (NDU),...
title: China’s PLA sets up new military academy colleges for AI, drones and discipline

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Around 150 Chinese language teachers in the Philippines are returning home following mounting criticism from Philippine security officials that educational exchanges involving China could pose national security threats.
The withdrawal affects teachers stationed at schools including the Immaculate Conception Academy in Greenhills and Jubilee Christian Academy in Quezon City, both in Metro Manila, according to local media.
The Manila-based Chinese Commercial News reported on Friday that the...
title: Chinese language teachers leave the Philippines over safety fears

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Taiwan has hailed the much-delayed arrival of two F-16V fighter jets as a demonstration of continuing US military support, despite the summit between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump.
The two single-seat aircraft, which reached Chihhang Air Base in the eastern county of Taitung on Friday, are the first new F-16s received by the island since deliveries of its original F-16A/B fleet began in 1997.
Compared with the earlier versions, the F-16V configuration incorporates the...
title: Taiwan hails F-16V delivery as sign US support holds after Xi-Trump summit

author: Chao Kong
description:
Large-scale field trials across China show that irrigation water treated with natural minerals radiated by sunlight could dramatically increase the yields of several crops, according to Chinese scientists behind the experiments.
The team said the trials, including on rice, wheat, soybeans, peanuts, sweet potatoes, sugar cane and vegetables, improved photosynthetic efficiency.
Their study, conducted from Heilongjiang province in northeastern China to Hainan province in the south, recorded yield...
title: Crop outputs grew up to 100% in China’s big agricultural experiment: scientists

author: Jianlu Bi
description:
Not so long ago, Washington’s approach to relations with Beijing was anchored by a single assertive phrase: dealing “from a position of strength”. It was rooted in a unipolar mindset: a belief that the United States could dictate terms, manage competition unilaterally and demand compliance from a distance.
Yet, at their recent summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump formally established a new strategic framework: a “constructive strategic stability relationship based...
title: How the US went from ‘a position of strength’ to ‘gung-ho’ on China

author: Orange Wang,Carol Yang
description:
Zheng Yongnian is a political scientist in China and a government adviser. His academic work is mainly about contemporary China, particularly politics, the country’s transformation and its external relations.
SCMP Plus readers get early access to articles in the Open Questions series.
Many have offered a lukewarm assessment of the Xi-Trump summit in Washington, citing the lack of a breakthrough. What is your take?
There are two primary views right now. One is nihilism, which holds that China and...
title: Zheng Yongnian on what to expect from future Xi-Trump meetings

author: Ling Xin
description:
A small Singaporean research team has beaten scientists in China and the United States to build the world’s most accurate atomic clock.
The clock, built with a single ion of a rare earth metal element known as lutetium, is so precise that it would lose one second every 260 billion years – nearly 20 times the age of our universe.
It is about four times as accurate as the previous record holder, a calcium-ion clock developed by a Chinese Academy of Sciences team in Wuhan, and also surpasses an...
title: David vs Goliaths: Singapore builds most accurate clock ever, leaves US and China in dust

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
A meeting next month between the leaders of the world’s three biggest nuclear powers is possible but hinges on the three sides finding common ground and setting realistic expectations about outcomes, according to analysts.
National Day congratulations from Moscow to Beijing on Thursday fanned speculation that the leaders of China, Russia and the United States could meet at the Apec summit in Shenzhen next month.
In a letter to Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir...
title: Putin’s hopes for ‘productive’ Apec fuel talk of summit with Xi and Trump

author: Meredith Chen
description:
Online claims that archaeologists have identified the source of mercury in the mausoleum of Qin Shi Huang – China’s first emperor, who unified the country more than 2,000 years ago – have revived interest in ancient cinnabar sites in northwestern China’s Shaanxi province.
The claims, which sent related hashtags trending on social media late last month, centred on three sites in Xunyang where archaeologists last year found evidence of cinnabar mining, processing and transport during the pre-Qin...
title: Online claims revive mercury mystery around tomb of first Chinese emperor
